investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T19:46–19:54Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent pod creation never completed, blocking the entire remote-agents feature eval.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three checks, confirming the failure is at the VM-resource scheduling layer, not in the eval runner or API logic. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. Because the pod never became schedulable, the runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable VM slots for new pods.

[Likely] The cluster has only 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource label and the pod's node affinity/selector excludes the other 4 nodes, meaning there is no fallback scheduling path even when the 2 eligible nodes are under pressure.

[Possible] A surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) exhausted the VM resource pool just before or during this eval window, causing transient but complete resource exhaustion.

[Possible] One or more previously created remote-agent pods are stuck in a non-terminal state (e.g., not cleaned up after a prior eval run), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that are not being released.

[Lower likelihood] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec was recently tightened or the node labels on the 4 non-matching nodes were changed, reducing the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T19:46–19:54Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent pod creation never completed, blocking the entire remote-agents feature eval.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three checks, confirming the failure is at the VM-resource scheduling layer, not in the eval runner or API logic. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. Because the pod never became schedulable, the runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable VM slots for new pods.

[Likely] The cluster has only 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource label and the pod's node affinity/selector excludes the other 4 nodes, meaning there is no fallback scheduling path even when the 2 eligible nodes are under pressure.

[Possible] A surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) exhausted the VM resource pool just before or during this eval window, causing transient but complete resource exhaustion.

[Possible] One or more previously created remote-agent pods are stuck in a non-terminal state (e.g., not cleaned up after a prior eval run), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that are not being released.

[Lower likelihood] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec was recently tightened or the node labels on the 4 non-matching nodes were changed, reducing the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes had zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain unscheduled for 130–150 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, no runtime response was produced and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent from the eval result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity across the two nodes that carry that resource label. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote-agent pod fails at the scheduler before the container ever starts. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the kata peer-pods VM resource, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers pod creation; that pod is immediately rejected by the scheduler, so no agent identity, model, or runtime response is ever returned, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 266–270) cannot be satisfied.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or peer-pod VMs are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates for remote-agent pods. If those 2 nodes' kata.peerpods.io/vm quota is small, even modest concurrent usage exhausts capacity.

Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and not being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1916), reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.
Cluster autoscaler not provisioning additional kata-capable nodes in time, or no autoscaler configured for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type, leaving the 2-node pool as a hard ceiling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > requested) at the time of the eval run — this would rule out resource exhaustion as the cause and point to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration instead.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime immediately after the failure window with no infrastructure changes, which would suggest a transient scheduling blip rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod affinity/selector was changed and now only 0 nodes match (not 2), which would shift the primary cause from VM resource exhaustion to a selector misconfiguration.

Scheduler logs showing the pod was rejected for a reason other than Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., image pull failure, admission webhook rejection) — this would indicate the scheduler message is misleading.

A sibling check outside the remote-agents feature (e.g., local-agent-create) also failing with a scheduling error, which would suggest a broader cluster problem rather than a kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific exhaustion.
